name: Agent Zero
hosting: self-hosted with Docker; desktop launcher available
tagline: Open agent framework with a Dockerized Linux desktop, browser, documents, projects, and plugins.
overview: Agent Zero is an open agent framework for work that goes beyond chat, giving the agent a containerized Linux desktop, a browser, and file access. It is used by developers and teams whose agents need to operate real GUI software, edit documents alongside the user, and work across isolated projects.
features: Runs a full Linux XFCE desktop in a Docker container that the agent can operate, including GUI applications
Provides a browser with DOM annotation so users can click page elements to change, inspect, or comment on them
Supports live co-editing of Markdown and LibreOffice Writer, Calc, and Impress documents with the agent
Offers a plugin hub with over 100 community extensions for tools, memory systems, and workflow automation
Isolates projects with per-project instructions, memory, secrets, Git repositories, and model preferences
Bridges to the host machine through the A0 CLI connector to work on host files, repos, and terminals
Tracks workspace history with snapshots, diffing, and rollback of agent-driven file changes
Spawns focused subagents for research, analysis, or specialized tasks
Switches between named model presets and agent behavior profiles

name: Agenta
license: MIT core, separately licensed enterprise features
tagline: Open-source workspace for building AI coworkers and automations by chatting with them.
overview: Agenta is an open-source workspace where users build agents that automate work by chatting with them, connecting the needed applications, and improving them through feedback. It is used by teams that want to share agents with role-based access and run them on existing Claude or ChatGPT subscriptions or their own models.
features: Builds agents interactively by describing tasks in chat
Shares agents with team members with access controlled by role
Provides a shared workspace where users and agents work on files together
Runs agents in the background on schedules or on events from connected applications
Sets per-tool permissions and approval rules for actions background agents may run automatically
Traces every model and tool call, tracking model requests, token usage, and estimated costs
Keeps version history of agent configurations to compare changes over time
Switches between harnesses (Claude Code, Pi, Codex) and multiple LLM providers without rebuilding
Connects to over 1,000 apps via Composio plus MCP servers

name: Eigent
tagline: Desktop application for building and running a multi-agent workforce on local machines.
overview: Eigent is an open-source desktop application for building, managing, and deploying a workforce of AI agents that turn multi-step workflows into automated tasks. It is used by developers and teams who want local-first agent execution where files, credentials, and context stay on their own machine.
features: Coordinates multiple agents on complex workflows with parallel execution
Runs focused single-agent tasks such as research, writing, and debugging with one meta agent
Executes agents locally so files, credentials, and context stay under user control
Connects cloud APIs, enterprise gateways, or local inference as model backends
Schedules recurring workflows so agents run tasks at set times
Includes built-in browser and terminal toolkits for agent tasks
Integrates external tools via the Model Context Protocol (MCP)
Supports customizable agent skills for specialized workflows
Offers enterprise options including SSO and access control

name: Hermes Agent
tagline: Self-improving personal agent with skills, memory, scheduling, and messaging channel access.
overview: Hermes Agent is a personal AI agent from Nous Research that creates skills from experience, improves them during use, and keeps persistent knowledge across sessions. It is used by developers and individuals who run an agent on their own infrastructure and reach it from a terminal or messaging apps.
features: Accessible via CLI, Telegram, Discord, Slack, WhatsApp, Signal, and Email through a unified gateway
Creates skills from experience and improves them during use
Provides a terminal TUI with multiline editing, slash-command autocomplete, history, and streaming tool output
Recalls past sessions using FTS5 search with LLM summarization and user modeling
Runs scheduled automations with a built-in cron scheduler that delivers to any connected platform
Spawns isolated subagents for parallel workstreams
Supports multiple terminal backends including local, Docker, SSH, Singularity, Modal, Daytona, and Vercel Sandbox
Works with Nous Portal, OpenRouter, OpenAI, and custom model endpoints with a model switch command

name: Kuse Cowork
tagline: Model-agnostic desktop coworker for document and data tasks with local-first execution.
overview: Kuse Cowork is an open-source desktop application, built in Rust, for AI-assisted task automation across documents and spreadsheets with user-selected models. It is used by people who want local-first execution, their own API keys, and control over which model provider handles their data.
features: Works with Claude, GPT, local models, and custom APIs through bring-your-own-key configuration
Processes DOCX, PDF, PPTX, and XLSX files with integrated UI operations
Processes receipts and generates formatted expense reports
Merges multiple document drafts, amendments, and feedback into unified versions
Extracts and tags metadata from large document batches
Extracts themes, action items, and insights from meeting transcripts
Generates Excel files with working formulas
Creates slide decks from transcripts or rough outlines
Cleans and restructures messy datasets into standardized formats

name: LibreChat
tagline: Self-hosted AI chat platform with agents, code execution, and multi-provider model access.
overview: LibreChat is a self-hosted, open-source AI chat platform that brings multiple AI providers into one interface with agents, code execution, and content generation. It is used by individuals and organizations that want a private, multi-user chat deployment with enterprise authentication.
features: Connects local and remote AI providers including Anthropic, OpenAI, Azure, Google, Groq, and Mistral via custom endpoints
Runs code in a sandboxed interpreter supporting Python, Node.js, Go, C/C++, Java, PHP, Rust, and Fortran with file handling
Builds no-code custom AI agents with marketplace discovery and collaborative sharing
Searches the web to add retrieved information to AI context, with configurable reranking services
Creates React, HTML, and Mermaid artifacts in chat with fullscreen preview and export
Supports image upload and analysis and chatting with files across providers
Authenticates users with OAuth2, LDAP, and email login, with built-in moderation tools
Imports conversations from ChatGPT and Chatbot UI and exports as screenshots, markdown, text, or JSON
Manages users, groups, roles, and configuration overrides from a browser-based admin panel

name: LobeChat
tagline: Agent workspace that manages teams of AI agents across multiple models and plugins.
overview: LobeChat is an agent orchestration platform that organizes multiple AI agents into coordinated teams working across models and tools. It is used by individuals and developers who build, deploy, and collaborate with AI agents, either on the vendor's hosted service or self-hosted.
features: Manages, schedules, and reports on multiple agents across different LLMs
Supports models from OpenAI, Claude, Gemini, and other providers across modalities
Provides over 10,000 skills through a plugin ecosystem with MCP compatibility
Auto-configures ready-to-use agents from a user's description of their needs
Runs agent groups in collaborative workspaces with shared context and project-based organization
Offers multi-agent writing and refinement pages with shared context
Keeps a structured, user-editable personal memory of preferences
Deploys via Vercel, Docker, Zeabur, Sealos, and Alibaba Cloud with configurable environment variables
Supports plugin development with an SDK, templates, and community contributions

name: Open WebUI
tagline: Self-hosted AI platform for local and cloud models that can run entirely offline.
overview: Open WebUI is a self-hosted AI platform that provides one interface for local models via Ollama and OpenAI-compatible cloud APIs, and is built to run entirely offline. It is used by individuals and organizations that want self-managed AI infrastructure with multi-user access controls.
features: Connects OpenAI-compatible APIs and local Ollama models, including LMStudio, GroqCloud, Mistral, OpenRouter, and vLLM
Enforces role-based access control with user groups, LDAP/Active Directory, and OAuth/SCIM provisioning
Runs local RAG with 9 vector database options, hybrid BM25 plus vector search, and multiple extraction engines
Supports hands-free voice calls with multiple speech-to-text and text-to-speech providers
Generates and edits images through DALL-E, Gemini, ComfyUI, and AUTOMATIC1111
Provides team channels with threads, reactions, and access controls for collaboration with AI
Schedules prompt execution with calendar integration and persistent artifact storage
Emits OpenTelemetry traces, metrics, and logs for production observability
Extends via Filters, Actions, Pipes, Tools, and Skills with MCP and OpenAPI integration

name: OpenClaw
hosting: self-hosted on a device or server
tagline: AI assistant that runs on your devices and answers in the messaging channels you already use.
overview: OpenClaw is an AI assistant that runs on your own devices and connects models, tools, messaging channels, and companion apps through one gateway. It is used by a single operator or a small trusted team, as a personal assistant on one laptop or a shared deployment.
features: Connects to WhatsApp, Telegram, Slack, Discord, Google Chat, Signal, iMessage, and other messaging channels
Works with hosted and local model providers
Adds voice, Canvas, camera, screen, and device-local actions through companion apps and nodes
Extends capabilities with tools, skills, and plugins, including a plugin SDK
Provides a Control UI, CLI, and TUI for interaction and management
Offers sandboxing options and security guides for multi-user deployments
Deploys on macOS, Linux, Windows, and Docker
Pairs users on DM-capable channels with approval workflows for unknown senders

name: OpenWork
license: mixed, open-source and separately licensed portions
tagline: Desktop app for sharing AI workflows, skills, and connected services across agents and teams.
overview: OpenWork is a free desktop app for sharing AI workflows, positioned as an open-source alternative to Claude Cowork and Codex for macOS, Windows, and Linux. It is used by individuals and organizations that want to reuse skills and connected services across agents such as Claude Code, Cursor, and Codex.
features: Runs as a desktop application on macOS, Windows, and Linux
Exposes one OpenWork MCP that Codex, Claude Code, Cursor, and other compatible agents can attach to reuse the same skills
Creates and organizes workspaces, shared with teammates or kept private
Reuses skills, MCPs, and connected services across tools, teammates, and machines
Integrates Google Workspace and Microsoft 365 capabilities
Manages teams, access, desktop policies, and marketplace publishing through the OpenWork Den control plane
Provisions inference at scale and controls which members and teams can use each model provider
Imports Agent Plugins and Anthropic-compatible plugins to access their skills through the OpenWork MCP

name: OpenWorker
tagline: Open-source desktop AI agent that completes tasks across files, apps, and Slack on your machine.
overview: OpenWorker is a desktop AI agent that runs locally and produces finished deliverables such as documents, spreadsheets, reports, and web pages. It connects to workplace tools and is aimed at developers, security teams, and professionals who want an agent for everyday tasks with human oversight.
features: Produces deliverables such as documents, spreadsheets, reports, and web pages
Connects to 25+ tools including GitHub, Slack, Jira, Notion, Linear, Gmail, and Google Calendar
Supports MCP-compatible tools, terminal access, and local files
Runs scheduled automations such as morning briefs and weekly reports
Works with OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini, DeepSeek, and Ollama models using your own API keys
Keeps dangerous operations human-only through hard governance floors
Lets approval-gated actions graduate to standing rules over time
Keeps audit trails recording who did what and why
Ships as a desktop app for macOS and Windows with a browser-based alternative

name: Paperclip
tagline: Open-source orchestration server and UI for coordinating teams of AI agents toward shared goals.
overview: Paperclip is a Node.js server and React UI that acts as a management layer over external AI agents rather than an agent framework. It is used by teams who want multiple agents working autonomously toward organizational goals with budgets, approvals, and audit logging.
features: Assigns work through a ticket-based task system with persistent context across sessions
Models org charts with roles, reporting lines, and permissions for humans and agents
Enforces per-agent monthly token and cost budgets that pause work when exceeded
Wakes agents on heartbeat schedules to check for work and act autonomously
Isolates multiple organizations in a single deployment with separate audit trails
Provides board approval workflows, execution policies, and full audit logging
Manages org-wide shared skills, evals, and performance metrics
Stores secrets encrypted with scoped access controls
Integrates with OpenClaw, Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, bash, and HTTP-based agents

name: Agno
tagline: Python framework and runtime for building agents, serving them as an API, and managing them in a UI.
overview: Agno combines an SDK for building agents with the AgentOS runtime for running them as services and a web UI for managing the platform. It targets developers and teams who want to run agent platforms on their own infrastructure while keeping session, memory, and knowledge data in their own databases.

Serves agents through 50+ API endpoints with SSE and websockets
Ships 100+ integrations and pre-built toolkits including GitHub, Slack, and Postgres
Pulls live context from Slack, Drive, wikis, MCP, and custom sources
Exposes agents via Slack, Telegram, WhatsApp, Discord, AG-UI, and A2A interfaces
Supports human approval workflows with pauseable runs
Provides OpenTelemetry tracing, run history, and audit logs
Offers JWT-based RBAC with multi-user, multi-tenant isolation
Runs cron-based scheduling and background jobs, deployable via Docker, Helm, and major clouds

name: CAMEL
tagline: Python framework for building and studying multi-agent systems, tasks, and simulated environments.
overview: CAMEL is a research-oriented Python framework for building agents and multi-agent systems. It is used by researchers studying agent scaling behavior and by developers building autonomous agent applications and synthetic data pipelines.

Supports configurable agent types, roles, tasks, and model backends
Coordinates agent societies and role-playing scenarios with dynamic communication
Scales experiments to large numbers of agents for studying scaling behavior
Generates synthetic data via Chain-of-Thought, self-instruction, and self-improving methods
Provides retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) pipelines
Integrates tools and external services into agent workflows
Includes memory and storage mechanisms for agent state management

name: CrewAI
tagline: Python framework for role-based agent crews and event-driven task flows.
overview: CrewAI is a Python framework for building multi-agent workflows with both high-level abstractions and low-level APIs. Developers use it to combine crews of role-based agents with event-driven flows for automations that mix autonomous reasoning with explicit business logic.
features: Organizes agents into crews with specialized roles, collaboration, and dynamic delegation
Provides event-driven flows with state management and conditional branching
Supports sequential and hierarchical task processes
Integrates tools and external APIs into agent work
Includes memory systems and knowledge base support
Supports MCP and A2A protocols
Produces structured outputs as JSON or Pydantic models
Offers human-in-the-loop integration and checkpointing
Runs tasks asynchronously with state persistence between tasks

name: Dify
license: Dify Open Source License (Apache-2.0 based, with conditions)
tagline: Platform combining a visual workflow builder, RAG pipelines, and agents for LLM applications.
overview: Dify is a platform for developing LLM applications, combining workflow building, retrieval pipelines, and agent capabilities in one workspace. Teams use it to take AI applications from prototype to production, either self-hosted or on Dify Cloud.
features: Builds and tests AI workflows on a visual canvas
Provides a RAG pipeline from document ingestion to retrieval, extracting text from PDFs, PPTs, and other formats
Defines agents based on LLM function calling or ReAct with pre-built or custom tools
Ships 50+ built-in tools including Google Search, DALL-E, and Stable Diffusion
Integrates hundreds of proprietary and open-source LLMs from dozens of inference providers
Monitors application logs and performance with Opik, Langfuse, and Arize Phoenix integrations
Exposes applications through backend-as-a-service APIs
Deploys as cloud-hosted, self-hosted, or VPC installations

name: Flowise
license: Apache-2.0 core, separately licensed enterprise features
tagline: Visual drag-and-drop builder for AI agents and language-model workflows.
overview: Flowise is a visual builder for constructing AI agents and LLM workflows with a low-code interface. It is used by developers and organizations who want to assemble chatbots, RAG systems, and multi-agent flows without writing everything in code. The GitHub repository was archived in August 2026.
features: Builds agent flows through a drag-and-drop visual interface
Supports multi-agent systems
Provides retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) capabilities
Builds chatbots and workflow automations
Composed of a Node.js backend server, React frontend, and third-party component integrations
Built on LangChain with support for various third-party nodes
Self-hosts on AWS, Azure, GCP, Digital Ocean, Railway, Render, HuggingFace Spaces, and other platforms
Available as a managed service via Flowise Cloud

name: Haystack
hosting: library for self-managed applications; vendor cloud available
tagline: Python orchestration framework for retrieval pipelines, document processing, and agents.
overview: Haystack is an open-source AI orchestration framework for building production LLM applications in Python. Teams use it to build modular pipelines for retrieval, RAG, question answering, and agents with explicit control over each component.
features: Composes modular pipelines with explicit control over retrieval, routing, memory, and generation
Supports conditional logic, loops, and branches in pipeline flow
Runs synchronously or asynchronously with token-by-token streaming
Builds agents with lifecycle hooks such as before_llm, before_tool, and on_exit
Tracks step counts, token usage, and tool calls in agent runs

Supports models from OpenAI, Mistral, Anthropic, Cohere, Hugging Face, Google, Azure, AWS Bedrock, and local backends
Exposes pipelines as REST APIs or MCP servers through Hayhooks
Provides OpenAI-compatible chat completion endpoints

name: Langflow
tagline: Visual and code-based platform for building agents and workflows served as APIs or MCP servers.
overview: Langflow is a platform for building AI agents and workflows through a visual builder with full Python source access to components. Developers use it to prototype flows in an interactive playground and deploy them as APIs or MCP servers.
features: Builds flows in a visual builder interface

Tests flows in an interactive playground with step-by-step control
Deploys flows as an API or exports them as JSON for Python apps
Deploys flows as an MCP server so they become tools for MCP clients
Orchestrates multiple agents with conversation management and retrieval
Supports major LLMs and vector databases
Integrates observability tools including LangSmith and LangFuse

name: LangGraph
hosting: library for self-managed applications; vendor platform available

Supports long-running agent executions
Allows inspecting and modifying agent state at any point for human-in-the-loop oversight
Provides short-term working memory for ongoing reasoning
Provides long-term persistent memory across sessions

Offers deployment infrastructure for stateful, long-running workflows via the vendor platform

name: Letta
tagline: Framework and server for building stateful agents with persistent memory that learn over time.
overview: Letta is a platform for building agents that keep memory across conversations and improve over time. It runs as a server that can be self-hosted or used through Letta Cloud, which stores agent memory, identity, and conversation history. Developers use it through a terminal UI, desktop apps, a web interface, and a TypeScript SDK.
features: Gives agents persistent memory that carries across conversations
Runs as a local or self-hosted app server
Provides a terminal UI, desktop apps for macOS, Windows, and Linux, and a web interface

Offers a TypeScript Agent SDK for embedding agents in applications
Letta Cloud maintains agent memory, identity, and history across devices
Installable via npm as @letta-ai/letta-code

name: LlamaIndex
hosting: library for self-managed applications; vendor cloud available
tagline: Python data framework for building agentic LLM applications over documents and data.
overview: LlamaIndex is an open-source framework for building LLM applications that work over existing data. It provides data connectors, indexing, and retrieval interfaces, and is used by developers ranging from beginners using short high-level workflows to advanced users customizing lower-level APIs. Structures data as indices and graphs for use with LLMs
Provides a retrieval and query interface that returns knowledge-augmented output

Lower-level APIs allow customization of connectors, indices, retrievers, and query engines
LlamaParse cloud service adds parsing for 130+ formats and structured extraction

name: MetaGPT
tagline: Python multi-agent framework that assigns software-company roles to LLMs to complete tasks.

Supports multiple LLM providers

name: Pydantic AI

MCP support for external tool integration

Offers hundreds of plugins for databases, cloud storage, APIs, and notifications

name: n8n
tagline: Fair-code platform for building AI agents and workflows on a visual canvas with code.

name: Node-RED
tagline: Low-code, flow-based programming tool for wiring devices, APIs, and online services.

features: Builds applications by wiring nodes together in a browser-based flow editor
Processes event-driven data flows

name: Pipedream
tagline: Hosted integration platform for event-driven automations with prebuilt and custom code steps.
overview: Pipedream is a hosted integration platform for developers that connects apps and runs event-driven automations. Workflows are sequences of prebuilt actions or custom code steps triggered by HTTP requests, timers, or third-party service events.

name: Prefect
tagline: Python workflow orchestration framework for building resilient data pipelines.

tagline: Durable execution platform that runs workflows resiliently and retries failed operations.
